Late Payments, Grace Period & Account Suspension\n\nCloudScale maintains an automated, transparent escalation procedure for overdue enterprise accounts to ensure continuous operation while mitigating credit exposure:\n\n- Day 1 (Due Date Passes): The invoice becomes past due. The account automatically enters a 7-day grace\n\nperiod. During this 7-day period, full platform access and compute services continue with zero service degradation.\n\n- Day 3 & Day 6: Automated payment retry attempts are executed against primary and backup payment methods on file.\n- Day 8 (Email Overdue Warning): Upon expiration of the 7-day grace period, CloudScale transmits an automated formal Email Warning to the primary account owner and billing administrator stating the account is delinquent.\n- Day 14 Overdue (Read-Only Suspension): If payment is not settled by Day 14, the account is transitioned to Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.\n- Day 30 Overdue (Late Fee Assessment): A final default notice is dispatched, and a monthly late fee of 1.5% (or statutory limit) is assessed on the outstanding balance.\n- Day 45 Overdue (Account Termination): If outstanding balances remain unpaid on Day 45, the account is formally terminated, and all active cloud computing workloads are immediately shut down.\n- Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.\n- Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.\n\nTable 1: Delinquency Escalation Schedule and System Actions\n\n| Overdue Day   | Account Status       | Operational Impact                                           | Notification & Required Action                               |\n|---------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Days 1-7      | 7-Day Grace Period   | Full platform access; CloudScale maintains an automated, transparent escalation procedure for overdue enterprise accounts to ensure continuous operation while mitigating credit exposure:

- Day 1 (Due Date Passes): The invoice becomes past due. The account automatically enters a 7-day grace

Late Payments, Grace Period & Account Suspension

CloudScale maintains an automated, transparent escalation procedure for overdue enterprise accounts to ensure continuous operation while mitigating credit exposure:

- Day 1 (Due Date Passes): The invoice becomes past due. The account automatically enters a 7-day grace

period. During this 7-day period, full platform access and compute services continue with zero service degradation.

- Day 3 & Day 6: Automated payment retry attempts are executed against primary and backup payment methods on file.
- Day 8 (Email Overdue Warning): Upon expiration of the 7-day grace period, CloudScale transmits an automated formal Email Warning to the primary account owner and billing administrator stating the account is delinquent.
- Day 14 Overdue (Read-Only Suspension): If payment is not settled by Day 14, the account is transitioned to Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.
- Day 30 Overdue (Late Fee Assessment): A final default notice is dispatched, and a monthly late fee of 1.5% (or statutory limit) is assessed on the outstanding balance.
- Day 45 Overdue (Account Termination): If outstanding balances remain unpaid on Day 45, the account is formally terminated, and all active cloud computing workloads are immediately shut down.
- Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.
- Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.

CloudScale maintains an automated, transparent escalation procedure for overdue enterprise accounts to ensure continuous operation while mitigating credit exposure:

- Day 1 (Due Date Passes): The invoice becomes past due. The account automatically enters a 7-day grace

period. During this 7-day period, full platform access and compute services continue with zero service degradation.

- Day 3 & Day 6: Automated payment retry attempts are executed against primary and backup payment methods on file.
- Day 8 (Email Overdue Warning): Upon expiration of the 7-day grace period, CloudScale transmits an automated formal Email Warning to the primary account owner and billing administrator stating the account is delinquent.
- Day 14 Overdue (Read-Only Suspension): If payment is not settled by Day 14, the account is transitioned to Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.
- Day 30 Overdue (Late Fee Assessment): A final default notice is dispatched, and a monthly late fee of 1.5% (or statutory limit) is assessed on the outstanding balance.

- Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.
- Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.
